title: Police shooting shocks family and neighbours of dead man
article: Family and friends of a man shot and killed by police say they're shocked by the confrontation.
Saskatoon city police went to Keldon McMillan's house on Sunday evening to arrest him. The incident spun into a highway chase that ended with a gun battle and McMillan's death.

"He wasn't a criminal," said Deanne Kasokeo a cousin of McMillan. "They shot him down like he was a criminal." Kasokeo told CBC that contrary to what Saskatoon police said on Sunday, McMillan was a status indian from Poundmaker Cree Nation.
"I strongly believe the justice system has to change," said Kasokeo. "The relations between First Nations and police services has to change."
The police chief, Dave Scott said he's confident his officers did the right thing. The RCMP is handling the internal investigation.
Meanwhile, neighbours of McMillan were recalling what led up to the shooting.
Dawn Dembrowski has known the McMillans for two years. She knew McMillan had lost his business, but said there weren't any signs of violence.

Until this Sunday, when police arrived to arrest McMillan over a domestic dispute. "One police officer ran across our yard and he had a gun and he just looked at me and said 'you get back in your house right now'. And I just, at that point I got scared."
McMillan then jumped into his truck and sped off. He was shot during a confrontation near Wakaw.
Police say he shot and killed a police dog, then pointed the gun at them.
